{{nihongo|'''Takaoka Sekino Shrine'''|高岡関野神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Etchū Province]].

'''Takaoka Sekino Shrine''' (たかおかせきのじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Suehiro-cho|ja|末広町 (高岡市)|qid=Q135477385|lt=Suehiro-cho}}, {{ill|Takaoka, Toyama|ar|تاكاوكا (توياما)|azb|تاکائوکا، تویاما|ce|Такаока|ceb|Takaoka Shi|cs|Takaoka|de|Takaoka|eo|Takaoka (urbo)|es|Takaoka (Toyama)|eu|Takaoka (Toyama)|fa|تاکائوکا، تویاما|fi|Takaoka|fr|Takaoka|hy|Տակաոկա|id|Takaoka, Toyama|it|Takaoka|ja|高岡市|ko|다카오카시|mg|Takaoka|ms|Takaoka, Toyama|my|တခအိုခ၊ တိုယာမ|mzn|تاکائوکا، تویاما|nl|Takaoka|no|Takaoka|pl|Takaoka|pt|Takaoka|ro|Takaoka|ru|Такаока|sh|Takaoka|simple|Takaoka, Toyama|sr|Такаока|sv|Takaoka|tg|Такаока|th|ทากาโอกะ|tl|Takaoka, Toyama|tr|Takaoka|tt|Такаока|uk|Такаока (Тояма)|vi|Takaoka, Toyama|war|Takaoka, Toyama|zh|高岡市|zh_classical|高岡市|zh_min_nan|Takaoka-chhī|zh_yue|高岡|qid=Q502988}}, {{ill|Toyama Prefecture|Q132929|qid=Q132929}}. The old orthography is '''Takaoka Sekino Jinja''' (關野), and another name is '''Taka-no-miya'''. Its former rank was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
There are three main sanctuary buildings, each enshrining the following deities.

* Shinmei Shrine ({{ill|Kuni-no-Tokotachi|ca|Kunitokotatchi|es|Kunitokotachi|fr|Kunitokotachi|it|Kuni-no-Tokotachi|ja|国之常立神|mni|ꯀꯨꯅꯤ-ꯅꯣ-ꯇꯣꯀꯣꯇꯆꯤ|ru|Куни-но токотати-но микото|simple|Kuni-no-Tokotachi|th|คูนิ โนะ โทโกตาจิ|uk|Куні но токотаті но камі|zh|國常立尊|qid=Q478504|lt=Kunitokotachi-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|bcl|Ukemochi|ca|Uke Mochi|da|Ogetsu-no-hime|de|Ukemochi|eo|Uke Moĉi|es|Uke Mochi|eu|Ukemochi|fa|اوکه موچی|hr|Uke Mochi|it|Uke-Mochi|ja|保食神|mni|ꯎꯀꯦꯃꯣꯆꯤ|pl|Ukemochi|pt|Ukemochi|ru|Укэмоти-но ками|sl|Uke-moči|sv|Uke-Mochi|uk|Укемоті|zh|保食神|qid=Q2280323}}, {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amateru Omikami}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mikeiri-no-Mikoto}})
* Kumano Shrine ({{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}, Kotosakanoo-no-Mikoto, Hayamizu-no-Mikoto), with aiden deities (Susanoo-no-Mikoto, Kagutsuchi)
* Inari Shrine ({{ill|Ukanomitama|de|Ukanomitama|eo|Ukanomitama|fr|Uka-no-Mitama|ja|ウカノミタマ|mni|ꯎꯀꯅꯣꯃꯤꯇꯃ|ru|Ука-но митама|simple|Ukanomitama|sv|Ukanomitama|th|อูกาโนมิตามะ|zh|宇迦之御魂神|qid=Q3080728|lt=Inakura-tama-no-Mikoto}} ({{ill|Inari Ōkami|Q719665|qid=Q719665|lt=Inari Omikami}}), {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|Q382005|qid=Q382005}}, {{ill|Maeda Toshinaga|ca|Maeda Toshinaga|es|Maeda Toshinaga|fa|مائدا توشیناگا|fr|Maeda Toshinaga|it|Maeda Toshinaga|ja|前田利長|ko|마에다 도시나가|ru|Маэда Тосинага|zh|前田利長|qid=Q1186742}})

=== History ===
Until the Edo period, Takaoka Sekino Shrine consisted of three shrines - Kakumi Shrine (Shinmei Shrine), Sekino Shrine (Kumano Shrine), and Takaoka Shrine (Inari Shrine) - collectively called the Sekino Three Shrines.

'''Kakumi Shrine''' (かくみじんじゃ) is said to have been a shikinaisha small shrine in Kamiseki Village, Sekino-go (present Kamiseki, Takaoka). However, another candidate for Kakumi Shrine exists in Kojiro, {{ill|Himi, Toyama|Q646886|qid=Q646886}}, and there is a tradition that when this shrine attempted to raise a plaque reading "Kakumi," parishioners from Himi's Kakumi Shrine came and prevented its use.

'''Sekino Shrine''' (せきのじんじゃ) began in {{ill|1604|Q6738|qid=Q6738}} (Keicho 9), when a divided spirit was transferred from Kumano-san Mitsuzo-ji in {{ill|Mitoda|Q11548628|qid=Q11548628}} (present {{ill|Imizu|Q851411|qid=Q851411}} Mitoda 3934), {{ill|Imizu District, Toyama|fa|ناحیه ایمیزو، تویاما|ja|射水郡|ko|이미즈군|zh|射水郡|qid=Q6004195}}, and enshrined as {{ill|Kumano Gongen|ja|熊野権現|simple|Kumano Gongen|zh|熊野權現|qid=Q11568925|lt=Kumano-gu}}<ref>[https://yaokami.jp/1166527/]、[http://www.mikumano.net/ztoyama/daimon1.html National Kumano Shrine Pilgrimage Record]、[http://www.kimura-product.co.jp/hudou1/hokurikuhudo36/hokurikuhudo3605.htm (Hokuriku 36 Fudo sacred sites)]</ref>.

'''Takaoka Shrine''' (たかおかじんじゃ) began in {{ill|1610|Q6765|qid=Q6765}} (Keicho 15), when Maeda Toshinaga invited Inari Omikami as castle guardian during construction of {{ill|Takaoka Castle|Q8011764|qid=Q8011764}}. It received devotion from the ruling {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Maeda family}} of the {{ill|Kaga Domain|Q903448|qid=Q903448}}, and later Toshinaga's spirit was also enshrined.

In {{ill|1806|Q6903|qid=Q6903}} (Bunka 3), Kakumi Shrine, Sekino Shrine, and Takaoka Shrine were moved to the current site and enshrined in one shared precinct. In Meiji, Kakumi Shrine was merged into Sekino Shrine and ranked as a gosha. Takaoka Shrine became a prefectural shrine. In {{ill|1919|Q2157|qid=Q2157}} (Taisho 8), Takaoka Shrine was merged into Sekino Shrine, creating the prefectural Takaoka Sekino Shrine.

=== Former Seki Residence ===
A two-story wooden building (priest residence) east of the shrine, thought to have been built in the {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} period. It is owned by the Seki family, hereditary chief priests of Sekino Shrine. It had been vacant since {{ill|1987|Q2429|qid=Q2429}}, but in {{ill|2022|Q49625|qid=Q49625}} the shrine acquired it and began utilizing it in cooperation with local construction company "KDC" and startup support company "Kaiju Ink." From autumn {{ill|2025|Q49616|qid=Q49616}} onward, it is being opened in stages as a mixed facility including lodging, restaurant, and souvenir shop. On November 1 of that year, a Japanese restaurant "Sekino" by kappo "Jubun" opened; souvenir shop and inn "tumuru" by ritual-goods maker "Hashimoto Kiyoshi" are scheduled for spring {{ill|2026|Q49613|qid=Q49613}} (shop) and winter of the same year (inn)<ref>From ''Toyama Shimbun'', Sep 20, 2025, p.25.</ref>.
